subject: Request: temporary subprocessor exception for APAC logging partner (Concordia)
messages:
From: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro.ruiz@concordiasystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Liao <maya.liao@concordia.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary subprocessor exception for APAC logging partner (Concordia)

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We have a production cutover planned for early Dec in Singapore and need to enable a partner-managed logging/observability agent that will forward redacted traces to our Concordia-managed observability cluster. That agent would be operated by Concordia Systems (third-party) and is not currently on Redwood's subprocessor roster.

Given the timeline, we're formally requesting a temporary exception (30 days) to allow Concordia's agent to run in APAC for the new customer rollout. We’ve attached a short justification and security brief (SOC2 excerpts, network diagram, and controls summary). Key points:
- Only redacted event-level telemetry will be sent (no PII, no raw prompt content).
- TLS in transit, mTLS between agent and Concordia endpoint.
- Data retention for forwarded events is 14 days; logs are purged automatically.

We need clarity on what evidence Redwood requires for a limited exception and whether a short addendum to the DPA is sufficient instead of a full subprocessor onboarding. Can we get an expedited review?

Files attached: concordia_temp_subproc_request.pdf; concordia_security_brief.zip

Appreciate any guidance—this is blocking our rollout schedule.

Best,
Alejandro Ruiz
Head of Integrations | Concordia Systems
alejandro.ruiz@concordiasystems.com
+65 8123 4455
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro.ruiz@concordiasystems.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary subprocessor exception for APAC logging partner (Concordia)

Alejandro —

Thanks for the note and for attaching the brief. I’ve looped in Naomi (privacy counsel), Irene (security engineering), and Kimberly (product ops) so we can triage. Short answers first: we can consider a short-term exception, but we need (1) a narrow scope & timeline, (2) explicit attestations, and (3) compensating controls while it’s in place.

Can you confirm the following so we can evaluate quickly:
1) Exact FQDNs/IPs the agent will talk to and whether Concordia will host endpoints inside SG region.
2) Formal data minimization statement signed by Concordia — fields that will never be forwarded (please list exact field names).
3) SOC2 or ISO27001 certificate pages (if available) and the specific control references for key rotation and breach notification SLAs.
4) A proposed exception duration (we typically consider 14/30 day windows for temporary exceptions).

Naomi — could you advise on whether a brief DPA addendum (time-boxed, limited scope) is acceptable vs. a full subprocessor onboarding? Irene — please flag any immediate redlines on the controls. Kimberly — I’ll need operational notes for deployment gating.

If you can get the items above by EOD tomorrow, we’ll aim for a review and decision within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
From: Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro.ruiz@concordiasystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Liao <maya.liao@concordia.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 02:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary subprocessor exception for APAC logging partner (Concordia)

Sean —

Appreciate the quick turn. Answers below and I’ve attached a slightly expanded packet (network_dataflow_v2.png is included):
1) Endpoints: prod-api.sg.concordia-observe.com (TLS, mTLS). Egress will be from Singapore region IP block 103.45.120.0/24.
2) Data minimization: agent will strip the following fields before forwarding: user_email, user_id, prompt_text, request_body. We will only forward event_type, timestamp, service_id, and aggregate metrics. Concordia signs that they will never request or store prompt_text or raw user content.
3) Attached: Concordia SOC2 summary (concordia_security_brief.zip) and the redacted attestation page. Key rotation: automated KMS rotation every 90 days; breach notification: 24h SLA to our security contact.
4) Proposed duration: 30 days with an automatic review at day 14. If all OK, we will submit to be added to Redwood's roster for standard onboarding.

Attachments referenced: concordia_temp_subproc_request.pdf; concordia_security_brief.zip; network_dataflow_v2.png

We’re ready to pause the rollout if any critical concerns arise, but we’re on a tight customer SLA so expedited approval would be ideal. Let me know if Naomi needs anything else for the DPA addendum.

Regards,
Alejandro
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary subprocessor exception for APAC logging partner (Concordia)

Team — forwarding the thread. Summary and decision: after reviewing the packet and speaking with security, we can approve a time-boxed exception under the following conditions: 
- Duration: 30 days from 2026-12-03 to 2027-01-01.
- Scope: Only the prod-api.sg.concordia-observe.com FQDN and the IP block 103.45.120.0/24 permitted.
- Data allowed: only event_type, timestamp, service_id, aggregate metrics (as attested). Explicit prohibition on storing prompt_text or request_body.
- Evidence: Concordia must provide (A) a signed short attestation PDF (we’ve attached a template), (B) SOC2 summary pages, and (C) periodic daily ingestion logs to be shared with Redwood security (redacted for PII) for the first 7 days.
- DPA addendum: Legal to sign a short addendum with the temp-exception clause and obligations above. Addendum must be executed before 2026-12-03 09:00 PST.

If Concordia signs and sends the attestation + we receive the addendum executed by 09:00 PST on 12/03, Security will enable the exception and Product Ops will open a gated rollout path. Any deviation will require immediate suspension.

Kimberly — please prepare the gated rollout checklist and the cutover holdback. Irene — confirm monitoring hooks and the daily log delivery endpoint for ingest reports. Sean — please send the attestation template to Alejandro and confirm timeline with the customer.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
